recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Handle any future W5/FiveWs mapping problems through focused resource- or mapping-specific Jira issues rather than reopening this broad FHIR-6304 umbrella.
issue_request: FHIR-6304 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It requested an abstract allowing easy extraction of action who, what, when, where, and why metadata attributes across all FHIR resources for Record Lifecycle Event needs, relying on a consistent metadata set.
initial_application: No direct FHIR-6304-tagged implementation commit was found. Source history instead shows broad W5/FiveWs infrastructure: the W5 subsystem was added in 2015, W5 QA checking was present by June 2015, and the FiveWs logical model was added to the active logical-model list in 2017.
additional_context: Current source keeps the legacy W5 map page in the build hierarchy but points it to the FiveWs pattern; source/fhir.ini actively lists fivews as a logical model; the FiveWs spreadsheet defines the cross-resource who/what/when/where/why concepts; source/sparql-rules.xml warns on missing W5 classifications. 2017 FHIR Workflow minutes support the pattern/logical-model interpretation, and later Jira/community searches show only separate resource-specific or unresolved W5 mapping items.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope source already embodies the W5/FiveWs classification framework, logical model, mappings, and QA process described by the issue resolution, and no bounded source correction is needed for this broad umbrella issue.
